target_customer: Social teams, performance marketers, agencies, creators and brands producing short-form paid video ads
problem: Making TikTok and Reels ads is slow and costly. Bluma lets users clone competitors' viral videos, recreate scripts and visuals, and edit in a canvas based editor.
business_model: SaaS subscription for an AI video ad tool (pricing requires a sales call per one review)

founders.name: Alisa Wu
founders.background_notes: YC page says she was a software engineer on self driving technology at Zoox.

technical_complexity.rationale: Pipeline that analyses viral videos and regenerates them with brand assets uses third party video models plus an editor and node canvas, standard engineering with heavy integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Many AI ad video tools exist and depend on shared underlying models; templates and a viral format library are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Comparison guides from 2026 list Creatify, Arcads and MakeUGC as established alternatives; no acquisition of Bluma was found.

market_need_then: Brands increasingly buy paid short-form video creative, and AI UGC tools were popular. No customer or revenue figures for Bluma were found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and practical, focused on speed and iteration

branding.community_and_virality: Has Product Hunt and YC launch posts; no brand press found

brand_strength.rationale: Short invented name, but near collisions with Luma AI, Bluma Wellness and the Blum crypto app, and no evidence of recall.

outcome_analysis: Bluma is a two person Fall 2025 company with a beta product that is free to try. No verified funding, revenue or outcome was found. The founders have engineering backgrounds, but the AI video ad category is crowded with established tools and defensibility is weak, so the story is unknown rather than failing.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and Extruct (aggregators) report about $500K via convertible note with Y Combinator; not recorded as a round. A Startup Daily article about a company called Lucent founded by an Alisa Wu is unrelated and ignored. No dated competitor sources near the Fall 2025 batch were found; results were 2026 comparison guides, so the list is empty. YC page claims NYT and SF Chronicle features for the CEO; a search could not confirm them. Completeness pass: The 500K dollar convertible note (stage other) rests on databases (CB Insights and Extruct) with no date; no press confirms it.
